# Scope, reproducibility, and review checkpoints

This document implements the quantitative analysis and figure-production workflow
for the revised AJBA body-form manuscript. It follows one chronological sequence:
**data import → non-destructive audits → descriptive statistics → inferential tests
→ sensitivity analyses → revised Figures 3–11 → session information**.
The superseded stature–body mass least-squares regression figure is not regenerated.


**Methodological preservation (2026-10-13 revision):** The selection of anatomical
records, formulas for stature/body mass/BMI/BI/CI/RBIB/TLLR, ANOVA-versus-Welch
decision rule, post hoc calculations, Kruskal–Wallis and Dunn tests, and
sex-specific dimorphism formula have not been deliberately changed. The original
analysis runs pairwise post hoc tests after an **unadjusted** significant
omnibus test; **Holm-adjusted omnibus significance** is required for the
Figures 3–5 brackets. Both flags are now exported for transparency. This
procedure needs author verification against the published Methods before release.

**Data use:** Only publish input CSVs when permissions allow. In particular,
check the rights and contextual sensitivity of the archaeological data. See
`README.md`, `data/README.md`, and `CHANGELOG.md` for provenance and decisions.
Run from the repository root using a fresh R session.

## Setup: packages, paths, and explicit switches

Relative input/output paths make the repository portable; raw CSVs are read,
not modified. Package **versions**, rather than just package names, should be
recorded with `renv::snapshot()` after a successful verified run.

```{r setup-packages-and-paths}

  "stringr", "scales", "knitr", "rmarkdown"
)

  !vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)
]

if (length(not_installed) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Install required R packages first: ",
    paste(not_installed, collapse = ", ")

}
```

## Additional Figure 9: separate input and controls (2026-10-27)

The original Figure 9 section and its `STAvsRLLL.csv` input are retained below.
The additional Figure 9 uses a **different** comparison table,
`data/ci_reference.csv`; do not replace or rename `STAvsRLLL.csv` to use it.
Both sections run in sequence and save figures under different filenames.

```{r figure-09-new-settings}
# Additional controls only; the original four-dataset import is unchanged.
RUN_FIG09_NEW <- TRUE
FIG09_NEW_CSV <- file.path(INPUT_DIR, "ci_reference.csv")

# FALSE plots the summaries supplied in ci_reference.csv without recomputing
# study values. TRUE refreshes study groups from main (dataset1/dataset2 only).
# Published reference rows and Sding Chung are retained from ci_reference.csv.
RECOMPUTE_FIG09_NEW_STUDY <- FALSE
```

The additional CSV must contain `Group`, `Sex`, `CI`, `CI_SD`, `CI_n`,
`Category`, and `Include_Figure9`. Use the revised comparison CSV supplied with
the new Figure 9 code. If it is missing, only the additional Figure 9 is skipped,
with a warning; the original Figure 9 and Figures 10–11 remain executable.

```{r import-source-data-and-audits}
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(
      tag, " missing fields: ", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", "),
      ". Check the CSV delimiter and column spelling."
    )
  }
}

# The original conversion of '-', blank, and textual missing values is kept.
as_num <- function(z) {
  x <- trimws(as.character(z))
  x[x %in% c("", "-", "NA", "N/A", "NaN")] <- NA_character_
  suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x))
}

# This audit does not alter any source data. It records which non-missing
# character tokens would become NA under the original as_num() function.
audit_numeric_conversion <- function(dat, columns, dataset_name) {
  columns <- intersect(columns, names(dat))

  purrr::map_dfr(columns, function(column) {
    original_text <- trimws(as.character(dat[[column]]))
    converted <- as_num(dat[[column]])

    known_missing <- is.na(original_text) |
      original_text %in% c("", "-", "NA", "N/A", "NaN")
    unexpected <- !known_missing & is.na(converted)

    if (!any(unexpected)) {
      return(tibble(
        dataset = character(), column = character(),
        row_number = integer(), original_value = character()
      ))
    }

    tibble(
      dataset = dataset_name,
      column = column,
      row_number = which(unexpected),
      original_value = original_text[unexpected]
    )
  })
}

region_label <- function(site) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    as.character(site) %in% c("PYDG", "BTXQ", "GL", "SDC") ~ "SCTP",
    as.character(site) == "PKGM" ~ "NTP",
    as.character(site) %in% c(
      "GS", "ZJZX_PreMing", "ZJZX_PostMing"
    ) ~ "Lowland",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}
```

```{r descriptive-tables}
summarise_trait <- function(dat) {
  dat %>% group_by(Site2, Region, Sex, Trait) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), mean = mean(Value), sd = sd(Value),
              median = median(Value), Q1 = unname(quantile(Value, .25)),
              Q3 = unname(quantile(Value, .75)),
              minimum = min(Value), maximum = max(Value),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(CV_percent = if_else(n >= 2 & mean != 0, 100 * sd / mean, NA_real_)) %>%
    arrange(Trait, Site2, Sex)
}
```

## Stature, body mass, BMI: omnibus tests and post hoc comparisons

Residual Shapiro–Wilk and Brown–Forsythe P values are **reported**. The original
analysis switches to Welch **only** when Brown–Forsythe P < 0.05; Shapiro–Wilk is
a diagnostic and does **not** select the test. These choices are preserved here
pending verification against the manuscript. Original pairwise tests follow a
raw-P < 0.05 omnibus; displayed brackets additionally require the Holm-adjusted
omnibus to be significant. Do not interpret all exported raw-gated pairwise rows
as Holm-confirmed findings.

```{r inferential-body-size}
# ==== 03 | SEX-SPECIFIC BODY SIZE: ANOVA, WELCH, TUKEY ======================
keep_replicated <- function(dat) dat %>%
  group_by(Site2) %>% filter(n() >= 2) %>% ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Site2 = droplevels(factor(Site2)))

# Median-centred Levene / Brown-Forsythe F-test in base R.
brown_forsythe_p <- function(dat) {
  dat <- dat %>% mutate(abs_dev = abs(Value - ave(Value, Site2, FUN = median)))
  as.numeric(summary(aov(abs_dev ~ Site2, data = dat))[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1])
}

# A Games–Howell test is used only if a Welch omnibus becomes significant;
# it handles heteroscedastic, unequal-n pairwise comparisons.
games_howell <- function(dat, trait, sex) {
  dat <- dat %>% group_by(Site2) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), avg = mean(Value), sd2 = var(Value), .groups = "drop")
  pairs <- combn(seq_len(nrow(dat)), 2, simplify = FALSE)
  purrr::map_dfr(pairs, function(idx) {
    a <- dat[idx[1], ]; b <- dat[idx[2], ]
    v1 <- a$sd2/a$n; v2 <- b$sd2/b$n
    sed <- sqrt((v1+v2)/2)
    nu <- (v1+v2)^2/(v1^2/(a$n-1)+v2^2/(b$n-1))
    diff <- b$avg-a$avg
    qv <- abs(diff)/sed
    p <- ptukey(qv, nmeans = nrow(dat), df = nu, lower.tail = FALSE)
    half <- qtukey(.95, nmeans = nrow(dat), df = nu) * sed
    tibble(Trait = trait, Sex = sex, Method = "Games-Howell",
           comparison = paste(b$Site2, a$Site2, sep = "-"),
           difference = diff, lower_95_CI = diff-half,
           upper_95_CI = diff+half, p_adjusted = p)
  })
}

run_body_tests <- function(body_dat) {
  omnibus <- list(); pairwise <- list(); c1 <- 0; c2 <- 0
  for (trait in c("Stature", "Bodymass", "BMI")) for (sex in c("M", "F")) {
    dat <- body_dat %>% filter(Trait == trait, Sex == sex) %>%
      keep_replicated()
    if (n_distinct(dat$Site2) < 2) next
    k <- n_distinct(dat$Site2)
    fit <- aov(Value ~ Site2, data = dat)
    f_tab <- summary(fit)[[1]]
    # A failed Shapiro test is a missing *diagnostic*, not a new test rule.
    p_normal <- if (length(residuals(fit)) >= 3 && length(residuals(fit)) <= 5000) {
      tryCatch(shapiro.test(residuals(fit))$p.value,
               error = function(e) NA_real_)
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
    p_bf <- brown_forsythe_p(dat)
    is_welch <- is.finite(p_bf) && p_bf < .05
    if (is_welch) {
      res <- oneway.test(Value ~ Site2, data = dat, var.equal = FALSE)
      test_name <- "Welch ANOVA"
      Fval <- unname(res$statistic)
      df1 <- unname(res$parameter[1]); df2 <- unname(res$parameter[2])
      pval <- res$p.value
    } else {
      test_name <- "One-way ANOVA"
      Fval <- unname(f_tab[["F value"]][1])
      df1 <- unname(f_tab[["Df"]][1]); df2 <- unname(f_tab[["Df"]][2])
      pval <- unname(f_tab[["Pr(>F)"]][1])
    }
    c1 <- c1 + 1
    omnibus[[c1]] <- tibble(Trait = trait, Sex = sex, Method = test_name,
                             groups_tested = k, n_tested = nrow(dat),
                             F = Fval, df1 = df1, df2 = df2,
                             p_raw = pval, shapiro_residual_p = p_normal,
                             brown_forsythe_p = p_bf,
                             compared_groups = paste(sort(unique(as.character(dat$Site2))), collapse = "; "))
    if (is.finite(pval) && pval < .05) {
      c2 <- c2 + 1
      if (is_welch) {
        pairwise[[c2]] <- games_howell(dat, trait, sex)
      } else {
        tkh <- as.data.frame(TukeyHSD(fit, "Site2")$Site2)
        pairwise[[c2]] <- tibble(Trait = trait, Sex = sex, Method = "Tukey HSD",
                                  comparison = rownames(tkh), difference = tkh[["diff"]],
                                  lower_95_CI = tkh[["lwr"]],
                                  upper_95_CI = tkh[["upr"]],
                                  p_adjusted = tkh[["p adj"]])
      }
    }
  }
  omnibus <- bind_rows(omnibus) %>% group_by(Sex) %>%
    mutate(p_Holm_3_traits = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm")) %>% ungroup()
  pairwise <- if (length(pairwise)) bind_rows(pairwise) else tibble(
    Trait=character(), Sex=character(), Method=character(),
    comparison=character(), difference=numeric(),
    lower_95_CI=numeric(), upper_95_CI=numeric(),
    p_adjusted=numeric())
  list(omnibus = omnibus, posthoc = pairwise)
}

body_tests <- run_body_tests(body_long)
write_csv(body_tests$omnibus, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Omnibus_body_size.csv"))
write_csv(body_tests$posthoc, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Posthoc_body_size_all_pairs.csv"))
write_csv(body_tests$posthoc %>% filter(p_adjusted < .05),
          file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Posthoc_body_size_significant.csv"))
```

## Brachial/crural indices and trunk-limb proportions: Kruskal–Wallis

Kruskal–Wallis is performed separately by sex for BI, CI and TLLR, with Holm adjustment across these three tests within sex. Sparse RBIB is primarily descriptive. When exactly two replicated groups are
available, the legacy analysis requests an exploratory Wilcoxon rank-sum test
with `exact = TRUE`; ties or package/R-version handling must be checked before
calling its output an *exact* P value. Dunn comparisons are still triggered by
the unadjusted Kruskal–Wallis P value; Holm status is separately audited.

```{r inferential-body-proportions}
# ==== 04 | BI, CI, TLLR: KRUSKAL–WALLIS & DUNN (IF SIGNIFICANT) ===========
dunn_pairwise <- function(dat, trait, sex) {
  # Tie-corrected Dunn's mean-rank comparisons, two-sided Holm-adjusted.
  N <- nrow(dat)
  ranks <- rank(dat$Value, ties.method = "average")
  freq <- table(dat$Value)
  tie_correction <- 1 - sum(as.numeric(freq)^3 - as.numeric(freq))/(N^3 - N)
  if (tie_correction <= 0) return(tibble())
  dat$rank_value <- ranks
  dat <- dat %>% group_by(Site2) %>%
    summarise(n = n(), avg_rank = mean(rank_value), .groups = "drop")
  pairs <- combn(seq_len(nrow(dat)), 2, simplify = FALSE)
  ret <- map_dfr(pairs, function(idx) {
    a <- dat[idx[1], ]; b <- dat[idx[2], ]
    z <- (b$avg_rank-a$avg_rank) /
      sqrt((N*(N+1)/12) * tie_correction * (1/a$n+1/b$n))
    tibble(Trait = trait, Sex = sex,
           comparison = paste(b$Site2,a$Site2,sep="-"),
           z = z, p_raw = 2 * pnorm(-abs(z)))
  })
  ret %>% mutate(p_Holm_pairs = p.adjust(p_raw, method="holm"))
}

kw_parts <- list(); dunn_parts <- list(); idx <- 0; didx <- 0
for (trait in c("BI", "CI", "TLLR")) for (sex in c("M", "F")) {
  dat <- prop_long %>% filter(Trait == trait, Sex == sex) %>% keep_replicated()
  k <- n_distinct(dat$Site2)
  if (k < 2) next
  kt <- kruskal.test(Value ~ Site2, data = dat)
  idx <- idx + 1
  kw_parts[[idx]] <- tibble(Trait = trait, Sex = sex,
    groups_tested = k, n_tested = nrow(dat),
    H = unname(kt$statistic), df = unname(kt$parameter), p_raw = kt$p.value,
    compared_groups = paste(sort(unique(as.character(dat$Site2))), collapse = "; "))
  if (kt$p.value < .05) {
    didx <- didx + 1
    dunn_parts[[didx]] <- dunn_pairwise(dat, trait, sex)
  }
}
kw_results <- bind_rows(kw_parts) %>% group_by(Sex) %>%
  mutate(p_Holm_3_traits = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm")) %>% ungroup()
dunn_results <- if (length(dunn_parts)) bind_rows(dunn_parts) else tibble(
  Trait=character(), Sex=character(), comparison=character(),
  z=numeric(), p_raw=numeric(), p_Holm_pairs=numeric())
write_csv(kw_results, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Omnibus_proportions_Kruskal_Wallis.csv"))
write_csv(dunn_results, file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Posthoc_Dunn_if_applicable.csv"))

# RBIB is sparse: descriptive primary; exact two-group rank-sum exploratory.
rbib_parts <- list()
for (sex in c("M", "F")) {
  dat <- prop_long %>% filter(Trait == "RBIB", Sex == sex) %>% keep_replicated()
  groups <- sort(unique(as.character(dat$Site2)))
  if (length(groups) != 2) next
  x <- dat$Value[as.character(dat$Site2) == groups[1]]
  y <- dat$Value[as.character(dat$Site2) == groups[2]]
  has_ties <- any(duplicated(c(x, y)))
  test <- wilcox.test(
    x, y, alternative = "two.sided", exact = TRUE, correct = FALSE
  )
  rbib_parts[[sex]] <- tibble(
    Sex = sex,
    group1 = groups[1],
    n1 = length(x),
    group2 = groups[2],
    n2 = length(y),
    W = unname(test$statistic),
    p_value = test$p.value,
    test_method_reported = test$method,
    ties_present = has_ties
  )
}
rbib_results <- if (length(rbib_parts) > 0) {
  bind_rows(rbib_parts)
} else {
  tibble(
    Sex = character(), group1 = character(), n1 = integer(),
    group2 = character(), n2 = integer(), W = numeric(),
    p_value = numeric(), test_method_reported = character(),
    ties_present = logical()
  )
}
write_csv(
  rbib_results,
  file.path(TABLE_DIR, "RBIB_exploratory_Wilcoxon.csv")
)
```

## Reusable figure themes, annotations

Shared site codes, colours and export settings are defined once.

```{r figure-design-and-export-helper}
# ==== 06 | FIGURE DESIGN / SAFE EXPORT HELPERS ============================
plot_theme <- theme_bw(base_size = 13) + theme(
  axis.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
  axis.text.x = element_text(size = 13, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
  axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14),
  strip.text = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 15),
  legend.position = "bottom",
  panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
  panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
)
export_figure <- function(plot, number, descriptor, width = 12,
                          height = 6.5) {
  # Use a common stem for all outputs; only raster TIFF has a DPI suffix.
  figure_stem <- sprintf("Figure_%02d_%s", number, descriptor)

  tiff_path <- file.path(
    FIGURE_DIR,
    sprintf("%s_%ddpi.tiff", figure_stem, TIFF_DPI)
  )

  ggsave(
    tiff_path,
    plot = plot,
    width = width,
    height = height,
    units = "in",
    dpi = TIFF_DPI,
    device = "tiff",
    compression = "lzw",
    bg = "white"
  )

  if (isTRUE(EXPORT_PDF)) {
    ggsave(
      file.path(FIGURE_DIR, paste0(figure_stem, ".pdf")),
      plot = plot,
      width = width,
      height = height,
      units = "in",
      device = "pdf",
      bg = "white"
    )
  }

  if (isTRUE(EXPORT_PNG_PREVIEW)) {
    ggsave(
      file.path(FIGURE_DIR, paste0(figure_stem, "_preview.png")),
      plot = plot,
      width = width,
      height = height,
      units = "in",
      dpi = 140,
      device = "png",
      bg = "white"
    )
  }

  message("Saved Figure ", number, ": ", tiff_path)
  invisible(tiff_path)
}
```

## Revised Figure 3-5: Stature, body mass and BMI

```{r figure-03-stature-data, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# ============================================================
# FIGURE 3 | Estimated stature
# ============================================================

# 1. Prepare stature data ------------------------------------

stature_dat <- body_long %>%
  filter(
    Trait == "Stature",
    Site2 %in% site_order,
    is.finite(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Site2 = factor(
      Site2,
      levels = site_order
    ),

    SexPanel = factor(
      Sex,
      levels = c("F", "M"),
      labels = c("Females", "Males")
    ),

    Region = factor(
      Region,
      levels = names(region_colors)
    )
  )


# 2. Prepare boxplots ----------------------------------------
# Only groups with n >= 3 receive boxplots.
# Groups with n = 1 or n = 2 remain as individual points.

stature_boxes <- stature_dat %>%
  group_by(Site2, SexPanel) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  ungroup()


# 3. Count observations --------------------------------------

stature_counts <- stature_dat %>%
  count(Site2, SexPanel, name = "n")


# 4. Determine panel-specific x positions --------------------

stature_panel_positions <- stature_dat %>%
  distinct(Sex, Site2) %>%
  arrange(Sex, Site2) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  mutate(
    x_position = row_number()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    Site2 = as.character(Site2)
  )


# 5. Determine Y-axis limits ---------------------------------

stature_min <- min(stature_dat$Value)
stature_max <- max(stature_dat$Value)

stature_bottom <- floor(stature_min - 4)
stature_top <- ceiling(stature_max + 3)

stature_n_y <- stature_min - 2.3


# 6. Extract significant pairwise comparisons ----------------
#
# Retain only comparisons for which:
#
# (1) The Holm-adjusted omnibus P < 0.05.
# (2) The pairwise-adjusted P < 0.05.
#
# The group identifiers are extracted directly from
# the comparison column in the post hoc results.

stature_sig <- body_tests$posthoc %>%
  filter(
    Trait == "Stature",
    p_adjusted < 0.05
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    body_tests$omnibus %>%
      filter(
        Trait == "Stature",
        p_Holm_3_traits < 0.05
      ) %>%
      select(Sex),
    by = "Sex"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    group1 = sub("-.*$", "", comparison),
    group2 = sub("^.*-", "", comparison)
  )


# 7. Assign correct panel-specific coordinates ---------------


stature_sig <- stature_sig %>%
  left_join(
    stature_panel_positions %>%
      transmute(
        Sex,
        group1 = Site2,
        x1 = x_position
      ),
    by = c("Sex", "group1")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    stature_panel_positions %>%
      transmute(
        Sex,
        group2 = Site2,
        x2 = x_position
      ),
    by = c("Sex", "group2")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(x1),
    !is.na(x2)
  )


# 8. Position significance brackets --------------------------

stature_sig <- stature_sig %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  arrange(
    p_adjusted,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y = max(
      stature_dat$Value[
        stature_dat$Sex == first(Sex)
      ]
    ) + 2.5 + (row_number() - 1) * 3.5,

    label = if_else(
      p_adjusted < 0.001,
      "P < 0.001",
      sprintf("P = %.3f", p_adjusted)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    SexPanel = factor(
      Sex,
      levels = c("F", "M"),
      labels = c("Females", "Males")
    )
  )


# 9. Check the bracket-to-group mapping ----------------------

# The actual comparison identifiers and numeric x positions
# are printed before generating the figure.

print(
  stature_panel_positions %>%
    arrange(Sex, x_position)
)

print(
  stature_sig %>%
    select(
      Sex,
      comparison,
      group1,
      group2,
      x1,
      x2,
      p_adjusted
    )
)


# 10. Optional significance annotations ----------------------

if (!isTRUE(SHOW_POSTHOC_BRACKETS)) {
  stature_sig <- stature_sig[0, ]
}


# 11. Extend Y-axis for brackets -----------------------------

if (nrow(stature_sig) > 0) {

  stature_top <- max(
    stature_top,
    max(stature_sig$y) + 3
  )
}
```

```{r figure-03-stature-plot}
    geom_segment(

}


# 4. Display figure ------------------------------------------

print(p_fig03)


# 5. Export figure -------------------------------------------
```

```{r figure-04-body-mass}
# ============================================================
# FIGURE 4 | Estimated body mass
# ============================================================
# 1. Prepare body mass data ----------------------------------

mass_dat <- body_long %>%
  filter(
    Trait == "Bodymass",
    Site2 %in% site_order,
    is.finite(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Site2 = factor(Site2, levels = site_order),
    SexPanel = factor(
      Sex,
      levels = c("F", "M"),
      labels = c("Females", "Males")
    ),
    Region = factor(
      Region,
      levels = names(region_colors)
    )
  )


# 2. Prepare boxplots ----------------------------------------
# Only groups with n >= 3 receive boxplots.
# Smaller groups remain visible as individual points.

mass_boxes <- mass_dat %>%
  group_by(Site2, SexPanel) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  ungroup()

# 3. Calculate sample sizes ----------------------------------

mass_counts <- mass_dat %>%
  count(Site2, SexPanel, name = "n")


# 4. Determine panel-specific site positions -----------------

mass_panel_positions <- mass_dat %>%
  distinct(Sex, Site2) %>%
  mutate(
    Site2 = as.character(Site2),
    site_rank = match(Site2, site_order)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Sex, site_rank) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  mutate(
    x_position = row_number()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-site_rank)


# 5. Extract significant post hoc comparisons ----------------
#
# Only comparisons satisfying both conditions are retained:
#
# (1) Holm-adjusted omnibus P < 0.05
# (2) Pairwise-adjusted P < 0.05
#
# The underlying ANOVA and post hoc test results
# are not modified.

mass_sig <- body_tests$posthoc %>%
  filter(
    Trait == "Bodymass",
    p_adjusted < 0.05
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    body_tests$omnibus %>%
      filter(
        Trait == "Bodymass",
        p_Holm_3_traits < 0.05
      ) %>%
      select(Sex),
    by = "Sex"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    group1 = sub("-.*$", "", comparison),
    group2 = sub("^.*-", "", comparison)
  )


# 6. Match comparisons to actual site positions --------------
#
# Numeric positions are used for arranging brackets
# and centring their P-value labels.

mass_sig <- mass_sig %>%
  left_join(
    mass_panel_positions %>%
      transmute(
        Sex,
        group1 = Site2,
        x1 = x_position
      ),
    by = c("Sex", "group1")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    mass_panel_positions %>%
      transmute(
        Sex,
        group2 = Site2,
        x2 = x_position
      ),
    by = c("Sex", "group2")
  )


# Do not silently discard unmatched comparisons.

if (anyNA(mass_sig$x1) || anyNA(mass_sig$x2)) {
  stop(
    "Figure 4: an adjusted significant comparison ",
    "does not match the displayed site groups."
  )
}


# Use factor levels consistent with the main x-axis.

mass_sig <- mass_sig %>%
  mutate(
    group1 = factor(group1, levels = site_order),
    group2 = factor(group2, levels = site_order)
  )


# 7. Determine sex-specific maximum body mass ----------------

mass_sex_max <- mass_dat %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    sex_max = max(Value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# 8. Position significance brackets --------------------------

mass_sig <- mass_sig %>%
  left_join(
    mass_sex_max,
    by = "Sex"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  arrange(
    abs(x2 - x1),
    p_adjusted,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y = sex_max + 1.5 +
      (row_number() - 1) * 2.6,

    label = if_else(
      p_adjusted < 0.001,
      "P < 0.001",
      sprintf("P = %.3f", p_adjusted)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    SexPanel = factor(
      Sex,
      levels = c("F", "M"),
      labels = c("Females", "Males")
    )
  )


# 9. Optional significance annotations -----------------------

if (!isTRUE(SHOW_POSTHOC_BRACKETS)) {
  mass_sig <- mass_sig[0, ]
}


# 10. Determine Y-axis limits --------------------------------

mass_min <- min(mass_dat$Value)
mass_max <- max(mass_dat$Value)

mass_bottom <- floor(mass_min - 3)
mass_top <- ceiling(mass_max + 3)

mass_n_y <- mass_min - 1.8

if (nrow(mass_sig) > 0) {
  mass_top <- max(
    mass_top,
    ceiling(max(mass_sig$y) + 2.5)
  )
}


# 11. Draw the main figure -----------------------------------

p_fig04 <- ggplot(
  mass_dat,

  # Boxplots for groups with n >= 3

  values = region_colors,

  drop = FALSE
) +

scale_fill_manual(
  name = "Region",
  values = region_colors,
  labels = region_labels,
  drop = FALSE
) +

  # Y-axis scale
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 7),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Estimated body mass (kg)"
  ) +

  plot_theme +

  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(mass_bottom, mass_top),
    clip = "off"
  )


# 12. Add sample-size labels ---------------------------------

if (isTRUE(SHOW_SAMPLE_N_ON_BOXPLOTS)) {

  p_fig04 <- p_fig04 +
    geom_text(
      data = mass_counts,
      aes(
        x = Site2,
        y = mass_n_y,
        label = paste0("n=", n)
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 4.8,
      colour = "grey35"
    )
}

# 13. Add significance brackets ------------------------------

if (nrow(mass_sig) > 0) {

  p_fig04 <- p_fig04 +

    # Horizontal bracket
    geom_segment(
      data = mass_sig,
      aes(
        x = group1,
        xend = group2,
        y = y,
        yend = y
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.45
    ) +

    # Left vertical tick
    geom_segment(
      data = mass_sig,
      aes(
        x = group1,
        xend = group1,
        y = y,
        yend = y - 0.4
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.45
    ) +

    # Right vertical tick
    geom_segment(
      data = mass_sig,
      aes(
        x = group2,
        xend = group2,
        y = y,
        yend = y - 0.4
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.45
    ) +

    # Adjusted P-value labels
    geom_text(
      data = mass_sig,
      aes(
        x = (x1 + x2) / 2,
        y = y,
        label = label
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      vjust = -0.4,
      size = 4.5
    )
}


# 14. Verify comparison-to-bracket mapping -------------------

cat("\n=== Figure 4: Site positions ===\n")

print(
  mass_panel_positions %>%
    arrange(Sex, x_position)
)

cat("\n=== Figure 4: Significant comparisons ===\n")

print(
  mass_sig %>%
    select(
      Sex,
      comparison,
      group1,
      group2,
      x1,
      x2,
      p_adjusted,
      y
    )
)


# 15. Display Figure 4 ---------------------------------------

print(p_fig04)


# 16. Export publication-quality figure ----------------------

export_figure(
  p_fig04,
  4,
  "Body_mass",
  width = 11,
  height = 7
)


# 17. Final Y-axis audit -------------------------------------

cat(
  "Body mass Y-axis:",
  mass_bottom,
  "to",
  mass_top,
  "kg\n"
)
```

```{r figure-05-bmi}
# ============================================================
# FIGURE 5 | Body mass index (BMI)
# Corrected panel ordering and significance annotations
# ============================================================


# 1. Prepare BMI data ----------------------------------------

bmi_dat <- body_long %>%
  filter(
    Trait == "BMI",
    Site2 %in% site_order,
    is.finite(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Site2 = factor(
      Site2,
      levels = site_order
    ),

    SexPanel = factor(
      Sex,
      levels = c("F", "M"),
      labels = c("Females", "Males")
    ),

    Region = factor(
      Region,
      levels = names(region_colors)
    )
  )


# 2. Prepare boxplots ----------------------------------------
# Boxplots only for groups with n >= 3.

bmi_boxes <- bmi_dat %>%
  group_by(Site2, SexPanel) %>%
  filter(n() >= 3) %>%
  ungroup()


# 3. Calculate sample sizes ----------------------------------

bmi_counts <- bmi_dat %>%
  count(Site2, SexPanel, name = "n")


# 4. Determine site positions by sex -------------------------

bmi_panel_positions <- bmi_dat %>%
  distinct(Sex, Site2) %>%
  mutate(
    Site2 = as.character(Site2),
    site_rank = match(Site2, site_order)
  ) %>%
  arrange(Sex, site_rank) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  mutate(
    x_position = row_number()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(-site_rank)


# 5. Identify significant comparisons ------------------------
#
# Both criteria must be met:
# (1) Holm-adjusted omnibus P < 0.05
# (2) Adjusted pairwise P < 0.05
#
# In the current full dataset, no BMI comparisons
# satisfy these conditions.

bmi_sig <- body_tests$posthoc %>%
  filter(
    Trait == "BMI",
    p_adjusted < 0.05
  ) %>%
  inner_join(
    body_tests$omnibus %>%
      filter(
        Trait == "BMI",
        p_Holm_3_traits < 0.05
      ) %>%
      select(Sex),
    by = "Sex"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    group1 = sub("-.*$", "", comparison),
    group2 = sub("^.*-", "", comparison)
  )


# 6. Match significant comparisons to site positions ---------

bmi_sig <- bmi_sig %>%
  left_join(
    bmi_panel_positions %>%
      transmute(
        Sex,
        group1 = Site2,
        x1 = x_position
      ),
    by = c("Sex", "group1")
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    bmi_panel_positions %>%
      transmute(
        Sex,
        group2 = Site2,
        x2 = x_position
      ),
    by = c("Sex", "group2")
  )


# Check for unmatched comparisons rather than dropping them.

if (anyNA(bmi_sig$x1) || anyNA(bmi_sig$x2)) {
  stop(
    "Figure 5: a significant comparison does not ",
    "match the displayed archaeological groups."
  )
}


# Use consistent site categories for bracket endpoints.

bmi_sig <- bmi_sig %>%
  mutate(
    group1 = factor(group1, levels = site_order),
    group2 = factor(group2, levels = site_order)
  )


# 7. Check the statistical results ---------------------------

if (nrow(bmi_sig) == 0) {

  message(
    "Figure 5: no Holm-confirmed significant ",
    "BMI pairwise comparisons. No brackets will be drawn."
  )
}


# 8. Determine sex-specific maximum BMI ----------------------

bmi_sex_max <- bmi_dat %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    sex_max = max(Value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )


# 9. Position brackets if significant results exist ----------

bmi_sig <- bmi_sig %>%
  left_join(
    bmi_sex_max,
    by = "Sex"
  ) %>%
  group_by(Sex) %>%
  arrange(
    abs(x2 - x1),
    p_adjusted,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    y = sex_max + 0.65 +
      (row_number() - 1) * 1.0,

    label = if_else(
      p_adjusted < 0.001,
      "P < 0.001",
      sprintf("P = %.3f", p_adjusted)
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    SexPanel = factor(
      Sex,
      levels = c("F", "M"),
      labels = c("Females", "Males")
    )
  )


# 10. Optional significance annotations ----------------------

if (!isTRUE(SHOW_POSTHOC_BRACKETS)) {
  bmi_sig <- bmi_sig[0, ]
}


# 11. Determine Y-axis limits --------------------------------

bmi_min <- min(bmi_dat$Value)
bmi_max <- max(bmi_dat$Value)

bmi_bottom <- floor(bmi_min - 1.2)
bmi_top <- ceiling(bmi_max + 1.2)

bmi_n_y <- bmi_min - 0.7

if (nrow(bmi_sig) > 0) {
  bmi_top <- max(
    bmi_top,
    ceiling(max(bmi_sig$y) + 1.0)
  )
}


# 12. Draw Figure 5 ------------------------------------------

p_fig05 <- ggplot(
  bmi_dat,
  aes(x = Site2, y = Value)
) +

  # Train x-axis using all valid BMI observations.
  geom_blank() +

  # Boxplots
  geom_boxplot(
    data = bmi_boxes,
    aes(
      colour = Region,
      group = Site2
    ),
    fill = NA,
    width = 0.53,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    linewidth = 0.75
  ) +

  # Individual observations
  geom_point(
    aes(fill = Region),
    shape = 21,
    colour = "grey25",
    size = 2,
    alpha = 0.82,
    stroke = 0.3,
    position = position_jitter(
      width = 0.085,
      height = 0,
      seed = 123
    )
  ) +

  # Separate females and males
  facet_wrap(
    ~SexPanel,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_x"
  ) +

  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = function(x) {
      site_order[site_order %in% x]
    },
    labels = function(x) unname(site_labels[x]),
    drop = TRUE
  ) +

  # Colours
scale_colour_manual(
  name = "Region",
  values = region_colors,
  labels = region_labels,
  drop = FALSE
) +

scale_fill_manual(
  name = "Region",
  values = region_colors,
  labels = region_labels,
  drop = FALSE
) +

  # BMI scale
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 7),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Body mass index (kg/m²)"
  ) +

  plot_theme +

  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(bmi_bottom, bmi_top),
    clip = "off"
  )


# 13. Sample-size labels -------------------------------------

if (isTRUE(SHOW_SAMPLE_N_ON_BOXPLOTS)) {

  p_fig05 <- p_fig05 +
    geom_text(
      data = bmi_counts,
      aes(
        x = Site2,
        y = bmi_n_y,
        label = paste0("n=", n)
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 4.5,
      colour = "grey35"
    )
}


# 14. Add brackets only if statistically justified -----------

if (nrow(bmi_sig) > 0) {

  p_fig05 <- p_fig05 +

    # Horizontal bracket
    geom_segment(
      data = bmi_sig,
      aes(
        x = group1,
        xend = group2,
        y = y,
        yend = y
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.45
    ) +

    # Left vertical tick
    geom_segment(
      data = bmi_sig,
      aes(
        x = group1,
        xend = group1,
        y = y,
        yend = y - 0.15
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.45
    ) +

    # Right vertical tick
    geom_segment(
      data = bmi_sig,
      aes(
        x = group2,
        xend = group2,
        y = y,
        yend = y - 0.15
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      linewidth = 0.45
    ) +

    # Adjusted P-value label
    geom_text(
      data = bmi_sig,
      aes(
        x = (x1 + x2) / 2,
        y = y,
        label = label
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      vjust = -0.45,
      size = 4.2
    )
}


# 15. Display Figure 5 ---------------------------------------

print(p_fig05)


# 16. Export publication-quality figure ----------------------

export_figure(
  p_fig05,
  5,
  "BMI",
  width = 11,
  height = 5.5
)


# 17. Check plotted range and comparisons --------------------

cat(
  "BMI Y-axis:",
  bmi_bottom,
  "to",
  bmi_top,
  "kg/m²\n"
)

print(
  bmi_sig %>%
    select(
      Sex,
      comparison,
      group1,
      group2,
      p_adjusted,
      x1,
      x2,
      y
    )
)
```

## Revised Figure 6: Trunk-to-lower-limb ratio

The trunk-to-lower-limb ratio (TLLR) is calculated from anatomical
height components and expressed as a dimensionless ratio.
Individual observations are displayed separately by sex.
Only site-sex groups with available TLLR observations are shown,
with sample sizes indicated beneath each archaeological group.

```{r figure-06-trunk-limb-ratio}
# ============================================================
# FIGURE 6 | Trunk-to-lower-limb ratio (TLLR)
# ============================================================


# 1. Prepare TLLR data ---------------------------------------
tllr_data <- prop_long %>%
  filter(
    Trait == "TLLR",
    Site2 %in% site_order,
    Sex %in% c("F", "M"),
    is.finite(Value)
  ) %>%
  mutate(

    # Preserve the predefined archaeological site order
    Site2 = factor(
      Site2,
      levels = site_order
    ),

    # Females on the left, males on the right
    SexPanel = factor(
      Sex,
      levels = c("F", "M"),
      labels = c("Females", "Males")
    ),

    # Regional classification
    Region = factor(
      Region,
      levels = names(region_colors)
    )
  )


# 2. Calculate sample sizes ----------------------------------


if (nrow(tllr_data) == 0) {
  stop("Figure 6: no valid TLLR observations available.")
}

tllr_counts <- tllr_data %>%
  count(
    Site2,
    SexPanel,
    name = "n",
    .drop = TRUE
  ) %>%
  filter(n > 0) %>%
  arrange(
    SexPanel,
    Site2
  )


# 3. Inspect sample sizes ------------------------------------

cat("\n=== Figure 6: TLLR sample sizes ===\n")

print(
  tllr_counts,
  n = Inf
)


# 4. Determine Y-axis limits ---------------------------------


tllr_min <- min(tllr_data$Value)
tllr_max <- max(tllr_data$Value)

tllr_range <- tllr_max - tllr_min

# Position sample-size labels below all observations
tllr_n_y <- tllr_min -
  max(tllr_range * 0.12, 0.018)

# Lower limit: leave room beneath sample-size labels
tllr_bottom <- tllr_n_y -
  max(tllr_range * 0.08, 0.015)

# Upper limit: a small margin above observations
tllr_top <- tllr_max +
  max(tllr_range * 0.06, 0.015)


# 5. Create Figure 6 -----------------------------------------

p_fig06 <- ggplot(
  tllr_data,
  aes(
    x = Site2,
    y = Value,
    colour = Region
  )
) +

  geom_point(
    size = 3,
    alpha = 0.9,
    position = position_jitter(
      width = 0.10,
      height = 0,
      seed = 456
    )
  ) +

  # Separate female and male panel

  facet_wrap(
    ~SexPanel,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_x",
    drop = TRUE
  ) +

  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = function(x) {
      site_order[site_order %in% x]
    },
    labels = function(x) {
      unname(site_labels[x])
    },
    drop = TRUE
  ) +

scale_colour_manual(
  name = "Region",
  values = region_colors,
  labels = region_labels,
  drop = FALSE
) +

  # Y-axis scale
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +

  # Axis labels
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Trunk-to-lower-limb ratio"
  ) +

  # Consistent manuscript figure theme
  plot_theme +

  # Include space for sample-size labels
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(tllr_bottom, tllr_top),
    clip = "off"
  )


# 6. Add sample-size labels ----------------------------------
#
# Display the number of valid observations
# beneath each archaeological group.

p_fig06 <- p_fig06 +

  geom_text(
    data = tllr_counts,
    aes(
      x = Site2,
      y = tllr_n_y,
      label = paste0("n=", n)
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    size = 4.5,
    colour = "grey35"
  )


# 7. Display Figure 6 ----------------------------------------

print(p_fig06)


# 8. Export publication-quality figure -----------------------

export_figure(
  p_fig06,
  6,
  "TLLR",
  width = 10,
  height = 5
)


# 9. Final plotting audit ------------------------------------

cat(
  "\nFigure 6 TLLR Y-axis:",
  round(tllr_bottom, 3),
  "to",
  round(tllr_top, 3),
  "\n"
)

cat("\nFigure 6: displayed sample sizes\n")

print(
  tllr_counts %>%
    select(
      SexPanel,
      Site2,
      n
    ),
  n = Inf
)
```

```{r figure-08-crural-index}
  geom_boxplot(
    data = ci_boxes,
    aes(
      colour = Region,
      group = Site2
    ),
    fill = NA,
    width = 0.56,
    linewidth = 0.8,
    outlier.shape = NA,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +


  geom_point(
    aes(fill = Region),
    shape = 21,
    colour = "grey25",
    size = 3,
    stroke = 0.3,
    alpha = 0.85,
    position = position_jitter(
      width = 0.08,
      height = 0,
      seed = 678
    )
  ) +

  # Sex-specific panels


  facet_wrap(
    ~SexPanel,
    nrow = 1,
    scales = "free_x",
    drop = TRUE
  ) +

  # Archaeological site labels

  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = function(x) {
      site_order[site_order %in% x]
    },
    labels = function(x) {
      unname(site_labels[x])
    },
    drop = TRUE
  ) +

  # Boxplot outline colours

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = region_colors,
    guide = "none"
  ) +

  # Individual observation colours
  #
  # Consistent with previous manuscript figures.

scale_fill_manual(
  name = "Region",
  values = region_colors,
  labels = region_labels,
  drop = TRUE
) +

  # Y-axis labels
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::breaks_pretty(n = 6),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
  ) +

  # Axis titles
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Crural index"
  ) +

  # Consistent manuscript figure theme
  plot_theme +

  # Plotting limits
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(ci_bottom, ci_top)
  )


# 9. Add sample-size labels ----------------------------------
#
# Display sample sizes only for site-sex groups
# with valid CI measurements.
#
# n = 1 and n = 2 groups are retained and labelled.
#
# Groups without observations are omitted.

if (isTRUE(SHOW_SAMPLE_N_ON_BOXPLOTS)) {

  p_fig08 <- p_fig08 +
    geom_text(
      data = ci_counts,
      aes(
        x = Site2,
        y = ci_n_y,
        label = paste0("n=", n)
      ),
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      size = 4.2,
      colour = "grey40"
    )
}


# 10. Display Figure 8 ---------------------------------------

print(p_fig08)


# 11. Export publication-quality figure ----------------------

export_figure(
  p_fig08,
  8,
  "Crural_index",
  width = 12,
  height = 6.3
)


# 12. Final plotting audit -----------------------------------

cat(
  "\nFigure 8 CI Y-axis:",
  round(ci_bottom, 2),
  "to",
  round(ci_top, 2),
  "\n"
)

cat("\nFigure 8: displayed site-sex groups\n")

print(
  ci_counts %>%
    select(
      SexPanel,
      Site2,
      n
    ),
  n = Inf
)
```


## Revised Figure 9: published comparative crural indices


```{r figure-09-published-CI-comparisons}
# ==== 10 | FIGURE 9: CRURAL INDEX, STUDY AND COMPARATIVE POPULATIONS =========
fig09_category_labels <- c(
  "Lowland" = "Lowland",
  "SCTP highland" = "Southern and Central Tibetan Plateau",
  "NTP highland" = "Northern Tibetan Plateau",
  "Reference sample" = "Reference sample"
)
# 1. Begin with the source already imported and validated in stage 01.
fig09_raw <- ref_raw %>%
  mutate(
    Group = trimws(as.character(Group)),
    Sex = trimws(as.character(Sex)),
    CI = as_num(CI)
  )

# 2. Preserve the published-data decision to exclude the pooled EU row.
fig09_data <- fig09_raw %>%
  filter(Group != "EU") %>%
  mutate(
    Sex = recode(Sex, "M" = "Male", "F" = "Female"),

    # Existing aliases are retained, including previously encountered
    # inconsistent separators and typographic spaces.
    Group_std = case_when(
      Group %in% c("ZJZXPre_Ming", "ZJZX_PreMing") ~ "ZJZXPre_Ming",
      Group %in% c("ZJZXPost_Ming", "ZJZX_PostMing") ~ "ZJZXPost_Ming",
      Group == "GS" ~ "GS",
      Group == "PYDG" ~ "PYDG",
      Group == "PKGM" ~ "PKGM",
      Group == "BTXQ" ~ "BTXQ",
      Group == "GL" ~ "GL",
      Group == "SDC" ~ "SDC",
      Group %in% c(
        "Highland Adean", "Highland   Adean", "Highland Andean"
      ) ~ "Highland Andean",
      Group == "NEU" ~ "NEU",
      Group == "SEU" ~ "SEU",
      Group %in% c("Arctic NA", "Arctic   NA") ~ "Arctic NA",
      Group %in% c("Tem NA", "Tem   NA", "Temperate NA") ~
        "Temperate NA",
      Group %in% c("GP NA", "GP   NA", "Great Plains NA") ~
        "Great Plains NA",
      TRUE ~ Group
    ),

    Group_label = case_when(
      Group_std == "ZJZXPre_Ming" ~ "Zhijiaozhongxin\n(pre-Ming)",
      Group_std == "ZJZXPost_Ming" ~ "Zhijiaozhongxin\n(post-Ming)",
      Group_std == "GS" ~ "Gaoshan",
      Group_std == "PYDG" ~ "Phiyang-Dungkar",
      Group_std == "PKGM" ~ "Pukar-Gongma",
      Group_std == "BTXQ" ~ "Putar Shongchu",
      Group_std == "GL" ~ "Gulie",
      Group_std == "SDC" ~ "Sding Chung",
      Group_std == "Highland Andean" ~ "Highland Andean",
      Group_std == "NEU" ~ "Northern Europe",
      Group_std == "SEU" ~ "Southern Europe",
      Group_std == "Arctic NA" ~ "North American Arctic",
      Group_std == "Temperate NA" ~ "Temperate North America",
      Group_std == "Great Plains NA" ~ "Great Plains North America",
      TRUE ~ Group_std
    ),

    Category = case_when(
      Group_std %in% c("ZJZXPre_Ming", "ZJZXPost_Ming", "GS") ~
        "Lowland",
      Group_std %in% c("PYDG", "BTXQ", "GL", "SDC") ~
        "SCTP highland",
      Group_std == "PKGM" ~ "NTP highland",
      TRUE ~ "Reference sample"
    ),

    Sample_type = if_else(
      Category == "Reference sample",
      "Comparative sample",
      "Study sample"
    )
  )


# 3. Audit original names, numeric CI and any source groups not on the axis.
group_order <- c(
  "Zhijiaozhongxin\n(pre-Ming)",
  "Zhijiaozhongxin\n(post-Ming)",
  "Gaoshan",
  "Pukar-Gongma",
  "Phiyang-Dungkar",
  "Putar Shongchu",
  "Gulie",
  "Sding Chung",
  "Highland Andean",
  "Northern Europe",
  "Southern Europe",
  "North American Arctic",
  "Temperate North America",
  "Great Plains North America"
)

write_csv(
  fig09_data %>%
    select(Group, Group_std, Group_label, Sex, CI, Category, Sample_type),
  file.path(AUDIT_DIR, "Figure_09_reference_source_and_mapping.csv")
)

unmapped_reference_groups <- fig09_data %>%
  filter(!Group_label %in% group_order | !Sex %in% c("Male", "Female"))
write_csv(
  unmapped_reference_groups,
  file.path(AUDIT_DIR, "Figure_09_unmapped_reference_groups.csv")
)

if (nrow(unmapped_reference_groups) > 0) {
  warning(
    "Figure 9 reference group or sex labels do not match the plot mapping. ",
    "Inspect Figure_09_unmapped_reference_groups.csv."
  )
}

fig09_data <- fig09_data %>%
  mutate(
    Group_label = factor(Group_label, levels = rev(group_order))
  )

# 5. Plot study groups and external comparative sample points.
p_fig09 <- ggplot(
  fig09_data,
  aes(x = CI, y = Group_label, colour = Category, shape = Category)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(80, 82, 84),

    colour = "grey85"
  ) +

scale_colour_manual(

    "NTP highland" = region_colors[["NTP"]],

) +

scale_shape_manual(

    "Lowland" = 16,

  ),

) +

guides(
  colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE),
  shape = guide_legend(nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
) +
  labs(
    x = "Crural index",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "white", colour = "black"
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    legend.position = "bottom",

  )

# 6. Display and export with the corrected revised-figure number.
print(p_fig09)
```

## Additional Figure 9: crural index point estimates and within-group SD

**Integration notes (2026-10-27).** The preceding Figure 9 code is preserved
verbatim, uses `ref_raw` imported from `STAvsRLLL.csv`, and produces
`p_fig09`. This additional version reads `FIG09_NEW_CSV` independently and
produces `p_fig09_new`; it does not reassign `ref_raw`, `fig09_raw`,
`fig09_data`, `p_fig09`, `group_order`, or the original input paths.

- Horizontal intervals represent **within-group standard deviations** (±1 SD),
  rather than standard errors or confidence intervals. Sample sizes are shown
  where available. The supplied `CI` values are used as point estimates.
- Sding Chung is displayed as a point estimate only. European reference
  estimates without SD are shown as open triangles. Missing SD values are
  not imputed.
- The four colour categories, larger text, one-row legend, and
  “Southern/Central Tibetan Plateau” display label follow the supplied new
  code. Source-table category names remain unchanged.
- `RECOMPUTE_FIG09_NEW_STUDY = FALSE` preserves the supplied comparison
  summaries. When enabled, only the listed study groups are refreshed from
  `main`, restricted to `dataset1`/`dataset2`, finite CI, and sex F/M.
  This optional refresh does not change `main` or either source CSV.
- Original exports keep the stem `Figure_09_Published_comparative_CI`.
  Additional exports use `Figure_09_CI_mean_SD`, with the shared `TIFF_DPI`,
  `EXPORT_PDF`, and `EXPORT_PNG_PREVIEW` settings. The plotted values and
  input-file hash for the additional dataset have separate audit filenames.

```{r figure-09-new-mean-SD-comparisons}
# ==== 10B | ADDITIONAL FIGURE 9: SEPARATE DATASET, POINT ESTIMATES +/- SD ====
if (!isTRUE(RUN_FIG09_NEW)) {
  message("Additional Figure 9 disabled (RUN_FIG09_NEW = FALSE).")
} else if (!file.exists(FIG09_NEW_CSV)) {
  warning(
    "Additional Figure 9 skipped: cannot find ", FIG09_NEW_CSV,
    ". Supply the revised ci_reference.csv; keep STAvsRLLL.csv for the original Figure 9.",
    call. = FALSE
  )
} else {
  fig09_new_output_dir <- FIGURE_DIR
  fig09_new_dpi <- TIFF_DPI

  # Separate provenance audit; the original four-input audit is unchanged.
  fig09_new_input_hash <- tibble::tibble(
    file_key = "figure09_new_reference",
    relative_path = FIG09_NEW_CSV,
    md5 = unname(as.character(tools::md5sum(FIG09_NEW_CSV)))
  )
  readr::write_csv(
    fig09_new_input_hash,
    file.path(AUDIT_DIR, "Figure_09_new_input_MD5.csv")
  )

  fig09_new_raw <- readr::read_csv(FIG09_NEW_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    rename_with(trimws)
  fig09_new_required_columns <- c(
    "Group", "Sex", "CI", "CI_SD", "CI_n", "Category", "Include_Figure9"
  )
  if (length(setdiff(fig09_new_required_columns, names(fig09_new_raw)))) {
    stop("Additional Figure 9 requires the revised ci_reference.csv. Missing columns: ",
         paste(setdiff(fig09_new_required_columns, names(fig09_new_raw)), collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (any(duplicated(fig09_new_raw[c("Group", "Sex")]))) {
    stop("The comparison CSV contains duplicate group-sex rows.")
  }

  # Optional: refresh the individual-level study summaries from the manuscript data.
  # Leave FALSE to plot the supplied, checked comparison CSV without other inputs.
  fig09_new_main_csv <- file_paths[["main"]]
  if (isTRUE(RECOMPUTE_FIG09_NEW_STUDY)) {
    # These metadata fields are used only for the optional study refresh.
    require_cols(
      fig09_new_raw,
      c("Group_label", "Sample_type", "Sta", "RLLL", "Sta_RLLL_status"),
      "Additional Figure 9 optional recomputation metadata"
    )
    fig09_new_study_sites <- c("PYDG", "BTXQ", "GL", "PKGM", "GS", "ZJZX_PreMing", "ZJZX_PostMing")
    if (exists("main", inherits = TRUE)) {
      fig09_new_master <- get("main", inherits = TRUE)
      fig09_new_master_source <- "Manuscript main object"
    } else {
      if (!file.exists(fig09_new_main_csv)) stop("Set file_paths[[main]] to your individual-level data file.")
      fig09_new_master <- read_csv(fig09_new_main_csv, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% rename_with(trimws)
      fig09_new_master_source <- fig09_new_main_csv
    }
    if (length(setdiff(c("Site2", "Sex", "Source", "CI"), names(fig09_new_master)))) {
      stop("Individual data must contain Site2, Sex, Source and CI.")
    }
    fig09_new_ci_text <- trimws(as.character(fig09_new_master$CI))
    fig09_new_ci_text[fig09_new_ci_text %in% c("", "-", "NA", "N/A", "NaN")] <- NA_character_
    fig09_new_ci_numeric <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(fig09_new_ci_text))
    if (any(!is.na(fig09_new_ci_text) & is.na(fig09_new_ci_numeric))) stop("Unexpected non-numeric CI token in main data.")
    fig09_new_master$CI <- fig09_new_ci_numeric
    fig09_new_summary <- fig09_new_master %>%
      filter(Source %in% c("dataset1", "dataset2"), Sex %in% c("F", "M"),
             Site2 %in% fig09_new_study_sites, is.finite(CI)) %>%
      group_by(Group = Site2, Sex) %>%
      summarise(CI = mean(CI), CI_SD = sd(CI), CI_n = n(), .groups = "drop")
    fig09_new_group_metadata <- fig09_new_raw %>%
      filter(Group %in% fig09_new_study_sites) %>%
      distinct(Group, Group_label, Category, Sample_type)
    fig09_new_legacy_columns <- fig09_new_raw %>% select(Group, Sex, Sta, RLLL, Sta_RLLL_status)
    fig09_new_updated_study <- fig09_new_summary %>%
      left_join(fig09_new_group_metadata, by = "Group") %>%
      left_join(fig09_new_legacy_columns, by = c("Group", "Sex")) %>%
      mutate(
        CI_statistic = if_else(CI_n > 1, "Mean of individual crural indices", "Single individual crural index"),
        SD_status = if_else(CI_n > 1, "Available", "Not estimable: n=1"),
        CI_source = fig09_new_master_source, CI_source_url = "",
        CI_source_location = "CI; Source in dataset1/dataset2; finite values; grouped by Site2 and Sex",
        Include_Figure9 = TRUE,
        Sta_RLLL_status = "Legacy columns retained for import compatibility; not used in Figure 9"
      )
    if (!nrow(fig09_new_updated_study) || anyNA(fig09_new_updated_study$Category)) {
      stop("No usable study CI values, or study group metadata is missing.")
    }
    fig09_new_raw <- bind_rows(filter(fig09_new_raw, !Group %in% fig09_new_study_sites), fig09_new_updated_study) %>%
      select(all_of(names(fig09_new_raw)))
    write_csv(fig09_new_raw, file.path(fig09_new_output_dir, "Figure_09_new_ci_reference_recomputed.csv"), na = "")
  }

  fig09_new_group_order <- c(
    "ZJZX_PreMing", "ZJZX_PostMing", "GS", "PKGM", "PYDG", "BTXQ", "GL", "SDC",
    "Highland Andean", "NEU", "SEU", "Arctic NA", "Temperate NA", "Great Plains NA"
  )
  fig09_new_group_labels <- c(
    ZJZX_PreMing = "Zhijiaozhongxin\n(pre-Ming)",
    ZJZX_PostMing = "Zhijiaozhongxin\n(post-Ming)",
    GS = "Gaoshan", PKGM = "Pukar-Gongma", PYDG = "Phiyang-Dungkar",
    BTXQ = "Putar Shongchu", GL = "Gulie", SDC = "Sding Chung",
    "Highland Andean" = "Ku\u00e9lap\n(Andean highlands)",
    NEU = "Northern Europe", SEU = "Southern Europe",
    "Arctic NA" = "North American Arctic",
    "Temperate NA" = "Temperate North America",
    "Great Plains NA" = "Great Plains\nNorth America"
  )
  fig09_new_colours <- c(
    "Southern and Central Tibetan Plateau" = "#D7301F",
    "Northern Tibetan Plateau" = "#7A3DB8",
    "Lowland" = "#2C7FB8",
    "Reference sample" = "#808080"
  )
  fig09_new_legend_labels <- c(
    "Southern and Central Tibetan Plateau" = "Southern/Central Tibetan Plateau",
    "Northern Tibetan Plateau" = "Northern Tibetan Plateau",
    "Lowland" = "Lowland",
    "Reference sample" = "Reference sample"
  )
  fig09_new_shapes <- c(
    "Southern and Central Tibetan Plateau" = 16,
    "Northern Tibetan Plateau" = 16,
    "Lowland" = 16, "Reference sample" = 17
  )

  fig09_new_data <- fig09_new_raw %>%
    filter(Include_Figure9, Group != "EU", is.finite(CI)) %>%
    mutate(
      SexPanel = factor(Sex, levels = c("F", "M"), labels = c("Females", "Males")),
      Category = factor(Category, levels = names(fig09_new_colours)),
      # Numeric rows keep identical group alignment in both sex panels.
      y_row = length(fig09_new_group_order) + 1L - match(Group, fig09_new_group_order),
      has_sd = is.finite(CI_SD) & !is.na(CI_n) & CI_n >= 2 & Group != "SDC",
      lower = if_else(has_sd, CI - CI_SD, CI),
      upper = if_else(has_sd, CI + CI_SD, CI),
      reference_point_only = Group %in% c("NEU", "SEU") & !has_sd
    )
  if (anyNA(fig09_new_data$y_row) || anyNA(fig09_new_data$SexPanel) || anyNA(fig09_new_data$Category)) {
    stop("Unrecognised group, sex or category in the comparison table.")
  }
  if (any(fig09_new_data$CI_SD < 0, na.rm = TRUE)) stop("Standard deviations must be non-negative.")
  if (any(is.finite(fig09_new_data$CI_SD) & !fig09_new_data$has_sd)) {
    stop("A supplied standard deviation is inconsistent with its sample size or estimate type.")
  }

  if (!nrow(fig09_new_data)) {
    stop("Additional Figure 9: no included finite CI point estimates to plot.")
  }

  fig09_new_x_min <- floor(min(fig09_new_data$lower)) - 0.5
  fig09_new_bar_end <- ceiling(max(fig09_new_data$upper)) + 0.5
  fig09_new_n_x <- fig09_new_bar_end + 0.78
  fig09_new_x_max <- fig09_new_bar_end + 2.5
  fig09_new_breaks <- seq(ceiling(fig09_new_x_min / 2) * 2,
                        floor(fig09_new_bar_end / 2) * 2, by = 2)

  p_fig09_new <- ggplot(fig09_new_data, aes(x = CI, y = y_row, colour = Category)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = fig09_new_breaks, colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.35) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 6.5, colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.4) +
    # Horizontal intervals are within-group SD, not SE or confidence intervals.
    geom_segment(data = filter(fig09_new_data, has_sd),
                 aes(x = lower, xend = upper, yend = y_row), linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_segment(data = filter(fig09_new_data, has_sd),
                 aes(x = lower, xend = lower, y = y_row - 0.12, yend = y_row + 0.12),
                 linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_segment(data = filter(fig09_new_data, has_sd),
                 aes(x = upper, xend = upper, y = y_row - 0.12, yend = y_row + 0.12),
                 linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(data = filter(fig09_new_data, !reference_point_only),
               aes(shape = Category), size = 3.4) +
    # Open triangles identify European estimates whose SD is unavailable.
    geom_point(data = filter(fig09_new_data, reference_point_only),
               shape = 2, size = 3.4, stroke = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_text(data = filter(fig09_new_data, !is.na(CI_n)),
              aes(x = fig09_new_n_x, label = paste0("n=", CI_n)),
              colour = "grey35", hjust = 0, size = 4, show.legend = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~SexPanel, nrow = 1) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      breaks = seq_along(fig09_new_group_order),
      labels = rev(unname(fig09_new_group_labels[fig09_new_group_order])),
      limits = c(0.3, length(fig09_new_group_order) + 0.7),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = fig09_new_breaks, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0))) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = fig09_new_colours, breaks = names(fig09_new_colours),
                        labels = fig09_new_legend_labels, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = fig09_new_shapes, breaks = names(fig09_new_colours),
                       labels = fig09_new_legend_labels, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE),
           shape = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE)) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(fig09_new_x_min, fig09_new_x_max), clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Crural index", y = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey97", colour = "grey40"),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      panel.spacing = grid::unit(0.8, "lines"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12.5, colour = "grey20"),
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12.5),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
      legend.position = "bottom", legend.text = element_text(size = 13),
      plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6)
    )


  print(p_fig09_new)
  fig09_new_stem <- file.path(fig09_new_output_dir, "Figure_09_CI_mean_SD")
  ggsave(paste0(fig09_new_stem, "_", fig09_new_dpi, "dpi.tiff"),
         plot = p_fig09_new, width = 12.6, height = 7, units = "in",
         dpi = fig09_new_dpi, device = "tiff", compression = "lzw", bg = "white")
  if (isTRUE(EXPORT_PDF)) {
    ggsave(paste0(fig09_new_stem, ".pdf"), plot = p_fig09_new,
           width = 12.6, height = 7, units = "in",
           device = if (capabilities("cairo")) grDevices::cairo_pdf else grDevices::pdf,
           bg = "white")
  }
  if (isTRUE(EXPORT_PNG_PREVIEW)) {
    ggsave(paste0(fig09_new_stem, "_preview.png"), plot = p_fig09_new,
           width = 12.6, height = 7, units = "in", dpi = 160, bg = "white")
  }
  write_csv(fig09_new_data,
            file.path(fig09_new_output_dir, "Figure_09_new_plotted_values.csv"), na = "")
  message("Additional Figure 9 saved to: ", normalizePath(fig09_new_output_dir))
}
```

## Revised Figure 10: relative bi-iliac breadth

Figure 10 retains the original calculation `100 × BIB / (10 × stature)`;

```{r figure-10-relative-bi-iliac-breadth}
# ==== 11 | FIGURE 10: RELATIVE BI-ILIAC BREADTH ==============================

# 1. Begin with the cleaned master dataset from the import stage.
# rename_with() was already applied to main_raw at import.
fig10_raw <- main

# 2. Define Figure-10-local order and labels; DO NOT overwrite site_order,
# site_labels, or region_colors used by later sections.
rbib_site_order <- c(
  "PYDG", "BTXQ", "GL", "PKGM", "ZJZX_PreMing"
)

rbib_site_labels <- c(
  PYDG = "Phiyang-Dungkar",
  BTXQ = "Putar Shongchu",
  GL = "Gulie",
  PKGM = "Pukar-Gongma",
  ZJZX_PreMing = "Zhijiaozhongxin\n(pre-Ming)"
)

# 3. Prepare individual values using the ORIGINAL Figure 10 formula.
fig10_data <- fig10_raw %>%
  filter(
    Source %in% c("dataset1", "dataset2"),
    Sex %in% c("F", "M"),
    Site2 %in% rbib_site_order
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Stature = as.numeric(na_if(as.character(Stature), "-")),
    BIB = as.numeric(na_if(as.character(BIB), "-")),

    # Convert centimetres to millimetres before standardisation.
    RBIB = BIB / (Stature * 10) * 100,

    Sex = factor(
      Sex, levels = c("F", "M"),
      labels = c("Females", "Males")
    ),

    Site2 = factor(
      Site2, levels = rev(rbib_site_order)
    ),

    Region = region_label(Site2),
    Region = factor(Region, levels = names(region_colors))
  ) %>%
  filter(is.finite(RBIB))

# 4. Calculate medians as a descriptive audit (not shown in Figure 10).
# Keep groups with at least 2 observations for this supplementary summary.
fig10_median_audit <- fig10_data %>%
  group_by(Site2, Sex) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%
  summarise(
    median_RBIB = median(RBIB),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

write_csv(
  fig10_median_audit,
  file.path(AUDIT_DIR, "Figure_10_RBIB_group_medians.csv")
)

# 5. The legacy display window is preserved, but report its coverage.
rbib_x_limits <- c(14.2, 18.4)
fig10_outside_window <- fig10_data %>%
  filter(RBIB < rbib_x_limits[1] | RBIB > rbib_x_limits[2])

write_csv(
  fig10_outside_window,
  file.path(AUDIT_DIR, "Figure_10_observations_outside_plot_window.csv")
)

if (nrow(fig10_outside_window) > 0) {
  warning(
    "Figure 10 has valid observations outside the published plot window. ",
    "Inspect Figure_10_observations_outside_plot_window.csv."
  )
}

# 6. Plot actual individual RBIB values without a fitted regression line.
p_fig10 <- ggplot(
  fig10_data,
  aes(x = RBIB, y = Site2)
) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = c(15, 16, 17, 18),
    colour = "grey85",
    linetype = "dotted",
    linewidth = 0.35
  ) +
  geom_jitter(
    aes(fill = Region),
    position = position_jitter(
      width = 0,
      height = 0.08,
      seed = 20261012
    ),
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.5,
    colour = "white",
    stroke = 0.45,
    alpha = 0.95
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Sex, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = function(x) unname(rbib_site_labels[x])
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(15, 16, 17, 18)
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = rbib_x_limits
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = region_colors,
    labels = region_labels,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Relative bi-iliac breadth (%)",
    y = NULL,
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold",
      margin = margin(t = 14)
    ),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    plot.margin = margin(5, 5, 5, 5)
  )

# 7. Display and export in the standard figures directory.
print(p_fig10)
export_figure(
  p_fig10, 10, "Relative_bi_iliac_breadth",
  width = 9, height = 5
)
```

## Revised Figure 11: within-trait sexual dimorphism

```{r figure-11-sexual-dimorphism}
# ==== 12 | FIGURE 11: WITHIN-TRAIT SEXUAL DIMORPHISM =========================

# 1. Original five site-period groups: NOT expanded without manuscript review.
sdi_sites <- c(
  "PYDG", "PKGM", "GS", "ZJZX_PreMing", "ZJZX_PostMing"
)

# 2. Compute sex-specific group means for each size measure.
sdi_long <- body_long %>%
  filter(Site2 %in% sdi_sites) %>%
  group_by(Site2, Trait, Sex) %>%
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean_value = mean(Value),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Sex,
    values_from = c(n, mean_value),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) %>%
  filter(
    is.finite(mean_value_M),
    is.finite(mean_value_F)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Symmetric male–female difference relative to the midpoint of means.
    # This is the ORIGINAL formula, not (M-F)/F or (M/F-1).
    SD_percent = 100 * (mean_value_M - mean_value_F) /
      ((mean_value_M + mean_value_F) / 2),

    Region = region_label(Site2),

    Sample_support = if_else(
      n_M < 2 | n_F < 2,
      "One sex n=1",
      "Both sexes n≥2"
    ),

    Trait = recode(
      Trait,
      Stature = "Stature",
      Bodymass = "Body mass",
      BMI = "BMI"
    ),

    Trait = factor(
      Trait, levels = c("Stature", "Body mass", "BMI")
    ),

    Site2 = factor(
      Site2, levels = rev(sdi_sites)
    ),

    Region = factor(
      Region, levels = names(region_colors)
    )
  )

# 3. Export full group means, sample sizes, and dimorphism percentages.
write_csv(
  sdi_long %>%
    mutate(
      Trait = as.character(Trait),
      Site2 = as.character(Site2)
    ),
  file.path(TABLE_DIR, "Sexual_dimorphism_group_means.csv")
)

# 4. Include x = 0 in all three facet ranges for interpretation.
zero_anchor <- tibble(
  Trait = factor(
    c("Stature", "Body mass", "BMI"),
    levels = c("Stature", "Body mass", "BMI")
  ),
  Site2 = factor(
    rep("PYDG", 3),
    levels = rev(sdi_sites)
  ),
  SD_percent = 0
)

# 5. Main plot. Global site labels and regional colours are untouched.
p_fig11 <- ggplot(
  sdi_long,
  aes(x = SD_percent, y = Site2)
) +
  geom_blank(
    data = zero_anchor,
    aes(x = SD_percent, y = Site2),
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    colour = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = Region, shape = Sample_support),
    size = 3.6,
    stroke = 1
  ) +
facet_wrap(
  ~Trait,
  nrow = 1,
  scales = "free_x",
  labeller = labeller(
    Trait = c(
      "Stature" = "Stature",
      "Body mass" = "Body mass",
      "BMI" = "Body mass index"
    )
  )
) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    labels = function(x) unname(site_labels[x]),
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%", accuracy = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.10, 0.14))
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = region_colors,
    labels = region_labels,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c(
      "Both sexes n≥2" = 16,
      "One sex n=1" = 1
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Male–female difference within trait (%)",
    y = NULL,
    colour = "Region",
    shape = "Sample representation"
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "grey95", colour = "grey60"
    ),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_text(size = 12.5, face = "bold"),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )

# 6. Display Figure 11 and export all configured formats.
print(p_fig11)
export_figure(
  p_fig11, 11, "Sexual_dimorphism",
  width = 12, height = 6
)
```
